pass_a_gloss: —then is for us against authorities that are not some visible and fleshly ones, and against world-rulers of the darkness that surrounds the human race, and against the spirits of wickedness that inhabit the heavenly place, that is, the air; and elsewhere at least he said, "in which you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, the spirit now at work in the sons of disobedience." For the air poured around us seems to be filled with opposing powers. Ephesians 6:13: "that you may be able to withstand," he says, "in the evil day." Origen: the one seeking to withstand in the evil day ought to have the full armor of God which the apostle set out, through which the adversary will be put to shame, having nothing base to say about us—the devil and accuser of our brothers, who also deceives sinners as his own and as having become of his portion. But another will say that the present age is an evil day. And a third account besides the two readings will say that the contest does not have an end for the one who has departed this life, but that even the one who has conquered here is about to contend also in another evil day against the opposing energies that appear. Ephesians 6:14: "Stand therefore, having girded your waist in truth." And in Luke it is written, "Let your waists be girded." What the belt is we now know: the one who has contracted the matters of generation and no longer serves it but hastens toward immortality girds the waist. Ephesians 6:14: "and having put on the breastplate of righteousness." Just as the one who has put on a breastplate is harder to wound when struck by enemies, and especially harder to wound in the more vital parts, so the one clothed with righteousness would not be wounded either as a deer struck in the liver by an arrow, nor fall into wrath or desire, but will also remain pure in heart, because he has put on the breastplate of righteousness forged for him by God the craftsman of all, who prepares and gives the full armor to each of the saints. Ephesians 6:15: "and having shod the feet in readiness of the gospel of peace." Notice that he named a certain power of the soul "feet," with which we as it were journey walking the one who said "I am the way," which feet one must shoe with the readiness of the gospel of peace. And I think symbols of these shoes are the shoes written in Exodus which those eating the Passover had to have, being ready for the journey. For so he says: "Eat it: your waists girded and your shoes on your feet and your staffs in your hands, and eat it with haste; it is the Lord's Passover." For readiness includes both eating with haste and eating while shod, so that strengthened by the foods they may be able to journey. So then the one journeying must be shod, but the one who has arrived at the holy land must untie: "Loose," he says, "the shoe from your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground." For this reason the one who is not yet an apostle must shoe the feet in readiness of the gospel of peace; but the apostle must no longer take shoes for a road, already perfected and being in the place where, standing and walking, he is on holy ground, living in Christ. Ephesians 6:16: "In all things taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the flaming arrows of the evil one." Origen says: the arrows of the evil one are evil reasonings; so he will not even be able at the start to cast into the heart, whenever someone is sheltered by the shield of faith, all the flaming arrows of the enemy being quenched in it; and the one wearing the shield of faith will say, "In the Lord I have trusted; how will you say to my soul, Migrate to the mountains like a sparrow? For behold, the sinners have stretched a bow; they have prepared arrows for a quiver, to shoot in a moonless place the upright in heart." For since I have trusted in the Lord, he says, how do you counsel me not to stand against the bows stretched against me by sinners and the arrows prepared by them in quivers, wanting to wound the upright in heart? For behold, I have also stood and I do not migrate, and all the flaming arrows of the evil one will be quenched almost at once. Ephesians 6:17b–19a: "and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, through every prayer and petition, praying in every season in the Spirit, and for this watching with all perseverance and—
pass_b_english: Our wrestling, then, is against authorities that are not visible and fleshly, against world-rulers of the darkness that wraps the human race, and against spirits of wickedness that inhabit the heavenly place—that is, the air. Elsewhere he said, "in which you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, the spirit now at work in the sons of disobedience." The air poured around us seems filled with opposing powers.

"That you may be able to withstand in the evil day" (Ephesians 6:13). Origen: whoever seeks to withstand in the evil day must have the full armor of God the apostle set out. Through it the adversary will be shamed, with nothing base to say about us—the devil, accuser of our brothers, who also deceives sinners as his own and as belonging to his portion. Another will say the present age is an evil day. A third reading, besides those two, will say the contest does not end when someone leaves this life: even the one who has conquered here is about to fight again in another evil day against opposing energies that appear.

"Stand therefore, having girded your waist with truth" (Ephesians 6:14). Luke also writes, "Let your waists be girded." We now know what the belt is: the one who has drawn in the works of generation, no longer serves them, and hastens toward immortality girds the waist.

"And having put on the breastplate of righteousness" (Ephesians 6:14). As a breastplate makes a fighter harder to wound—especially in the vital parts—so the one clothed with righteousness will not be struck like a deer hit in the liver by an arrow, will not fall into wrath or desire, and will remain pure in heart. He wears a breastplate of righteousness forged for him by God, the craftsman of all, who prepares and gives the full armor to each of the saints.

"And having shod your feet with the readiness of the gospel of peace" (Ephesians 6:15). Notice he named a power of the soul "feet," with which we journey, walking the one who said "I am the way." Those feet must be shod with the gospel's readiness for peace. I take the Exodus shoes required of those eating the Passover, ready for the road, as symbols of these: "Eat it with your waists girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staffs in your hands; eat it in haste; it is the Lord's Passover." Readiness includes both hasty eating and eating while shod, so that strengthened by the food they can travel. The one still journeying must be shod; the one who has reached the holy land must untie: "Loose the shoe from your feet, for the place where you stand is holy ground." So the one not yet an apostle must shoe the feet with the gospel's readiness for peace; the apostle no longer takes shoes for a road—already perfected, standing and walking on holy ground, living in Christ.

"In all things taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the flaming arrows of the evil one" (Ephesians 6:16). Origen: the evil one's arrows are evil thoughts. He cannot even begin to cast them into the heart when someone is covered by the shield of faith; all the flaming arrows are quenched in it. The one wearing that shield will say, "In the Lord I have trusted; how will you say to my soul, Flee to the mountains like a sparrow? For look, sinners have stretched a bow and prepared arrows for a quiver, to shoot the upright in heart in a moonless place." Since I have trusted in the Lord, how do you advise me not to stand against the bows and quivered arrows sinners aim, wanting to wound the upright in heart? Look: I have stood; I do not flee; and all the flaming arrows of the evil one will be quenched almost at once.
"And the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, through every prayer and petition, praying at every time in the Spirit, and watching for this with all perseverance and—" (Ephesians 6:17–19)

choices.english: the heavenly place, that is, the air
choices.why: Origen equates the 'heavenly' battlefield of Eph 6:12 with the surrounding air filled with opposing powers.
rejected: the stars as physical sky only
a purely metaphorical 'atmosphere' with no powers
